- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is falling sharply.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent high), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day of sentiment decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 7 days.
